author: i. a. coffin
title: Presbyterian softball shut out twice at Spring Break Challenge in Florida
text:
The Presbyterian College softball team began the Spring Break Challenge in Jacksonville, Florida, with two losses on Friday. The Blue Hose were defeated by Georgia Southern 8-0 in five innings and then fell to host Jacksonville 3-0.
After these results, Presbyterian’s season record stands at 11 wins and 11 losses. The team has struggled when playing away from home, holding a 4-5 record in road games so far this season. Despite leaving 12 runners on base across both games, the Blue Hose could not generate enough offense to score.
In the first game against Georgia Southern, the Eagles scored twice in the first inning and added three more runs in the third. They secured a run-rule victory with a two-run single in the fifth inning. Avery Robinson pitched 4.2 innings for Presbyterian and also contributed two hits at bat. Grace Kelley recorded the final out of the game.
During their second matchup against Jacksonville, Presbyterian was unable to produce any extra-base hits for a second consecutive contest but managed to out-hit Jacksonville six to four. Senior pitcher Peyton Duncan threw her 23rd complete game of her college career, allowing only one solo home run and two RBI groundouts while striking out four batters. However, offensive support was lacking as Presbyterian failed to reach base during their last seven at-bats.
Presbyterian will continue its weekend schedule with another game against Georgia Southern and a meeting with North Florida.
